subject: Throughput runbook + econ signoff (MAP draft)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie@finixpayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput runbook + econ signoff (MAP draft)

Hi Julie,

Thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (MAP) + throughput runbook focused on the performance gates you asked for: TTFT, tokens/sec (sustained and burst), and concurrency behavior at 95th pct. I also attached a simple unit-econ CSV with a couple of model/quantization permutations we discussed.

High-level summary (from runbook v1):
- Acceptance target: sustain 4,000 tokens/sec (aggregate) for your finance-workflow peak, with median TTFT <= 120 ms and 95th-pt TTFT <= 220 ms under target concurrency (40 concurrent user sessions).
- Burst capacity: short bursts to 8,000 tokens/sec with automatic fallback to a smaller variant when tail latency exceeds SLA for more than 30s.
- Unit econ: ~ $3.60 per 1M tokens served (hosted, mixed-precision profile A, with prefix cache on for common prompts). CSV has per-model delta.

Proposed MAP milestones (dates tentative):
1) Runbook acceptance (this doc) — target signoff: 2027-06-03 — owner: Finix (Julie) + Redwood (Vanessa).
2) Bench and repro tests in Finix staging — 2027-06-07 to 2027-06-09 — owner: Finix eng + Redwood bench team (Ben).
3) Performance tuning & quantization recommendation — 2027-06-10 to 2027-06-14 — owner: Redwood (Ben).
4) Final acceptance run and economics review — 2027-06-17 — owner: Finix (Julie) + Redwood (Marissa).
5) Contract signature and Reserved Capacity kickoff — 2027-06-21 — owner: Finix legal & Redwood sales.

Attachments: throughput_runbook_v1.pdf (details of test harness, traffic profiles, KV cache config), econ_summary_q2.csv (per-1M tokens costs), bench_results_0507.zip (preliminary internal runs from Redwood that motivated the targets).

Two asks from our side to keep the timeline:
- Can you confirm acceptance of the runbook targets by 2027-06-03? (Reply ok to this thread is fine.)
- Can your staging team provide a sample traffic trace (one hour of peak workload) or a synthetic traffic profile by 2027-06-05? That will let us tune batching and prefix cache settings before the bench window.

I'll follow up with a DocuSign link for the MAP once we have signoff so the milestone owners are explicit in the agreement.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0197
https://redwood.ai

(Attachment: throughput_runbook_v1.pdf, econ_summary_q2.csv)

From: Julie Park <julie@finixpayments.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts-payable@finixpayments.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput runbook + econ signoff (MAP draft)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the doc and clear milestones. A couple quick clarifications from our eng and finance teams:
- Can you confirm what you mean by TTFT (is that time-to-first-token server-side, or includes client RTT)? We need server-only numbers for comparison to our SLOs.
- For the sustained 4,000 tokens/sec target, what is the per-node concurrency and how many GPUs did you assume in the econ CSV?
- Finance wants a ballpark monthly run-rate delta if we commit to reserved capacity (25% uplift vs hosted), can you include a simple line-item in the econ CSV for \"25% reserved commit\"?

We can try to get the traffic trace by Friday. If possible, can we do a short sync with Ben to align on the bench harness details before the bench window?

—Julie
Julie Park
Sr. Eng Manager, Finix Payments
julie@finixpayments.com

(On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 09:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:...)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Park <julie@finixpayments.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput runbook + econ signoff (MAP draft)

Julie —

Quick answers inline and a short bench plan below.

TTFT definition: server-side TTFT (time from request received by API edge to first token emitted by the model). Our reported medians exclude client RTT. The numbers in the runbook use server-side instrumentation.

Hardware assumption (econ CSV): mixed cluster of A100-80GB equivalents. For the baseline sustained 4k tokens/sec we assumed 4 GPUs serving the model variant (mixed precision) with continuous batching and prefix cache enabled. Burst to 8k tokens/sec assumes autoscaling to 8 GPUs for short windows. We will add a \"25% reserved commit\" line to the CSV before final signoff.

Representative bench results (internal, trimmed):
- Model variant: rw-instruct-13B-quant-v2
- Median TTFT: 98 ms (95th pct: 185 ms) at 4,000 tokens/sec aggregate across 4 GPUs (40 concurrent sessions, each ~100 tokens/resp).
- Sustained tokens/sec (per GPU): ~1,000 tokens/sec sustained (continuous batching tuned; batching window 10–15 ms).
- Observed tokens/sec (burst): up to 2,100 tokens/sec per GPU for 30s (CPU/GPU headroom dependent).
- Cost (hosted mixed-precision): ~ $3.60 / 1M tokens (baseline) — reserved commit 25% estimated ~ $2.70 / 1M tokens (ballpark).

Bench plan (Finix staging window 2027-06-07 -> 2027-06-09):
- Day 1 (6/7): smoke run to validate harness, ensure KV prefix cache warm-up profile matches sample trace. (Owner: Finix eng + Redwood bench infra)
- Day 2 (6/8): sustained run at target 4k tokens/sec for 60 minutes; collect TTFT, tail latency, and token flow traces. (Owner: Redwood bench + Finix)
- Day 3 (6/9): stress/burst scenario (6k–8k tokens/sec windows) and A/B with quant profiles. (Owner: Redwood)

Deliverables after bench: raw traces, consolidated bench report (CSV + PDF), recommended deployment profile and estimated unit-econ with reserved-commit lines. We'll package results in bench_results_0507.zip and a short dashboard link.

Next steps I propose: short sync Friday 2027-06-04 at 10am PT to walk the harness and verify the trace format. I'll send a calendar invite; Vanessa, can you confirm?

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Bench Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0123
(Attachment: bench_results_0507.zip)

Julie —

Thanks for the quick replies and Ben for the details. That's helpful. From a CS acceptance perspective we'll mark the following as PASS/FAIL gates for the final acceptance on 2027-06-17:
- Functional correctness and no >1% regression in output quality against the sample eval set.
- Sustained tokens/sec >= 4k for 1 hour with median TTFT <= 120 ms and 95th <= 220 ms.
- No unhandled errors and <0.5% request failure rate during the acceptance window.

One small request from Finix: can we extend query log retention to 60 days for the acceptance window so their analysts can re-run traces? If legal is okay, Redwood can toggle retention on the private dataset for that period. Please confirm and we will reflect it in the DocuSign MAP.

I'll add the PASS/FAIL checklist to the shared Drive doc and include the final DocuSign link once Vanessa confirms we have signoff on the runbook doc.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
